SHIVENDRA JHA VILLAGE-MUJAUNA, PO- NIRPUR, PS- TAJPUR,

 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Ravindra Kumar, Adv.
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Manoj Kumar, APP  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SATYAVRAT VERMA  ORAL ORDER 2 16-01-2024 1.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned APP for the State.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the present quashing application has been filed seeking quashing of the order dated 09.08.2023 passed by the learned Sessions Judge,
Samastipur in Cr. Revision No.396/2023, whereby the order dated 26.06.2023 passed by the learned A.C.J.M.-1st, Samastipur in Domestic Violence Act Case No.40/2022, whereby cognizance of offence under Section 31 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as D.V. Act) has been taken stands Patna High Court CR.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: MISC. No.66184 of 2023(2) dt.16-01-2024 affirmed.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that for the present he is not making any submission on merits but only raises a short legal issue.

It is next submitted that the order dated 26.06.2023, by which cognizance of offence under Section 31(1) of the D.V. Act has been taken is not sustainable for the reason that it is not the case of the O.P. No.2 that any protection order passed Raj Kumar Choudhary vs The State Of Bihar on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45649958/
1 under Section 18 of the D.V. Act was violated rather the case of the O.P. No.2 is that an order passed under Sections 20 and 21 of the D.V. Act was breached, it is next submitted that even presuming what has been alleged by the O.P. No.2 is true that the order passed under Sections 20 and 21 of the D.V. Act was breached but then the same does not give rise to any criminal offence for which cognizance can be taken under Section 31 of the D.V. Act as Section 31 of the D.V. Act incorporates-Penalty for breach of protection order by respondent.

sentences.text: (1) A breach of protection order, or of an interim protection order, by the respondent shall be an offence under this Act and shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both.

(2) The offence under sub-section (1) shall as far as practicable Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.66184 of 2023(2) dt.16-01-2024 be tried by the Magistrate who had passed the order, the breach of which has been alleged to have been caused by the accused.

(3) While framing charges under sub-section (1), the Magistrates may also frame charges under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or any other provision of that Code or the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961), as the case may be, if the facts disclose the commission of an offence under those provisions.
4.

The learned counsel for the petitioner thus submits that as per mandate of Section 31(1) of the D.V. Act, 2005, cognizance of offence can be taken for violation of the protection order and not for breach of an interim order of maintenance passed under Section 20 of the D.V. Act and an order passed under Section 21 of the D.V. Act for grant of custody of the child to the O.P. No.2 herein.

It is next submitted that plain reading of Section 18 of the D.V. Act, in light of the definition, as incorporated under Section 2(O) of the D.V. Act, it can be safely inferred that order granting maintenance and custody of child does not amount to protection order, hence violation of the same will not attract provision of Section 31 of the D.V. Act.

It is next submitted that if grant of maintenance and custody of child under Sections 20 and 21 of the D.V. Act would have been inclusive of the protection order, then provision for granting protection order under Section 18 of the Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.66184 of 2023(2) dt.16-01-2024 D.V. Act would not have been incorporated separately.

The learned counsel for the petitioner reiterates his submission and submits that cognizance of an offence can be taken under Section 31 of the D.V. Act, 2005 only if the protection order passed under Section 18 of the D.V. Act is violated.
5. The learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 seeks three weeks time for filing a counter affidavit.

6. Put up this case on 11.03.2024.
7.

In the meantime, the order dated 09.08.2023 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Samastipur in Cr. Revision No.396/2023, whereby the order dated 26.06.2023 passed by the learned A.C.J.M.-1st, Samastipur in Domestic Violence Act Case No.40/2022, whereby cognizance of offence under Section 31 of the Act has been taken, has been affirmed, shall remain stayed.
